description: Certificate Signing Request | Document sent to a CA to apply for a digital certificate. Contains the applicant's public key and identity details; private key stays secret.
Certificate Revocation List | A published list of revoked/invalid certificates published periodically by a CA. Main drawback: caching delays cause latency in detecting revoked certs.
Online Certificate Status Protocol | Real-time query mechanism to check certificate revocation status. Fast alternative to CRLs, but can create privacy and performance bottlenecks.
Web server queries OCSP server directly and 'staples' the time-stamped OCSP response to the TLS handshake, protecting user privacy and reducing CA server load.
Top-level Certificate Authority. Kept offline in a secure vault to prevent compromise. Signs Intermediate CA certificates.
Subordinate CA trusted by the Root CA to issue day-to-day end-entity certificates. If compromised, it can be revoked without invalidating the Root CA.

protocol: Single vs Hierarchical vs Web of Trust
description: Architecture determining trust paths. Hierarchical (Root -> Intermediate -> Leaf) is the standard enterprise and internet model.
Third-party storage of cryptographic keys. Ensures an organization can recover encrypted data if an employee leaves or loses their decryption key.
Hardcoding expected certificate keys into an app to block Man-in-the-Middle attacks. Deprecated due to high risk of accidental lockouts.
